analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/developer/build.md (head text only, with no diff markers) and docs/developer/test.md (metadata unit 67373c0eff1153bd:0 plus patch unit :1). No runtime, coordinator, provider, auth or crypto code is modified, so there is no security behavior change.

build.md (lines ~444-1258) describes the pinned MLX/SDK submodule revisions, the build steps, the App Attest release qualification procedure (lines 1114-1160), and the advisory threat-model review tooling (1224-1237).
- The documented text says qualification is artifact-bound and that publication, approval and signing remain separate outcomes.
- Native verifier and canonical backend docs are explicitly kept in the sibling darkbloom-platform repository.
- The text does not claim that the TB-011, T-053 or T-054 controls changed.
- The threat-model review tooling is documented as treating PR content as data and never building or executing PR code. It uses an Actions secret and a trusted base checkout. That is consistent with the untrusted-input stance and introduces no new attack surface.

test.md patch: test hygiene (disabling Git maintenance and GC in disposable repos, Trace2 verification) and landing-site test descriptions. The landing tests use local HTTP upstreams and need no production credentials. It also states that a passing local suite is not live verification, which is appropriately cautious.

The PR is not mapped to T-041 or the other threats. The pin table for libs/mlx-swift-lm and libs/mlx-swift cites PR numbers and commit hashes. Their correctness (matching the actual gitlinks) was not verifiable from the supplied unit text, which is a coverage limit rather than a finding. Nothing in this PR requires a threat-model update.
